instruction: Change the font of all text in this document to Times New Roman.

parameters.window_name: 04 CHIN9505 EBook Purchasing info 2021 Jan.docx - LibreOffice Writer

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to use tabstops to split sentences (first 3 words left, rest right). Successfully navigated Format > Paragraph > Tabs dialog and set a right-aligned tab stop at 15cm. Failed when manually editing each line to insert tabs: text concatenation errors, partial completion, unintended formatting changes.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Writer menus (Format > Paragraph), open dialogs, select all text (Ctrl+A), use toolbar formatting options, type text, use keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z)
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at precise text manipulation: inserting tab characters mid-line caused text concatenation, undo didn't fully restore state, and manual line-by-line editing was error-prone. Only completed partial lines with some getting unintended bold/red formatting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single-operation font change task. Model demonstrated it can select all text and access formatting menus, so changing font is within its capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting all text and changing font to Times New Roman. Getter reads the docx file and checks both the default style font and individual run fonts. Metric gives 0.5 for correct default style font and 0.5 for all runs having the correct font.

scoring_breakdown.default_style_font: 0.5 - Default/Normal style font is Times New Roman
scoring_breakdown.run_fonts: 0.5 - All text runs use Times New Roman font

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts both the Normal style default font and all individual run fonts from the docx file using python-docx, which is the right state to verify the instruction.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('expected_font'), receiving the rules dict as expected.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Coverage is complete: the single instruction requirement (change all text font to Times New Roman) is verified by checking both default style font and individual run fonts.
Case-insensitive font name comparison is appropriate for robustness.

Minor: Getter uses set() for run_fonts, so partial credit is calculated over unique font names rather than individual runs. This means one mismatched font among many correct runs penalizes more harshly than a per-run ratio would, but for a task requiring 'all text' to be changed, stricter checking is acceptable.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider collecting run fonts as a list (with duplicates) instead of a set, so partial credit ratio reflects the actual proportion of correctly-formatted runs rather than unique font names.
